title: Check yourself: Connectors, integrations and working safely

questions.stem: A manager links the company's cloud storage, then asks Claude to summarise a restricted finance directory. Claude cannot find it, although an administrator colleague sees it in the same storage. What explains this?

options.text: The tool carries the signed-in person's rights, which exclude that location
options.says: "Claude inherits each person's permissions from the connected service", so the manager's reach, not the administrator's, decides what appears.

options.text: The tool reads only material above a certain age, and that area is newer
options.says: Ruled out because the page names permissions as the cause of a missing result ("the connector cannot reach it from Claude for them either") and says nothing about the age of material.

options.text: The workspace holding the chat must be shared before the area becomes visible
options.says: Ruled out because "Fixing a connector's reach is done in the source system", not by sharing a workspace.

options.text: The area is too big for retrieval to cope with in a single request
options.says: Ruled out because the page ties a missing result to access, as in "the connector cannot reach it from Claude for them either", and never to size.

questions.stem: A company connects its helpdesk to Claude. Agents may read tickets and add internal notes freely, but ending a ticket must wait for a person's click, and trainees must not see escalated tickets. Which design meets both rules?

options.text: Require approval to close, and write the group's limit into the connector's instructions
options.says: Ruled out because "Fixing a connector's reach is done in the source system, by changing who can open what, not by rewording an instruction".

options.text: Allow every tool without approval and expect the helpdesk to stop the trainees
options.says: Ruled out because an organisation can "let Claude read a system and require a human click before it writes to it", and always allowing every tool gives that up.

options.text: Require approval to close, and leave the group's limit in the source system itself
options.says: Each tool can be set to need approval, and Claude inherits each person's permissions, so a restriction on one group belongs in the source system.

options.text: Require approval to close, and give that group wider access through Claude's settings
options.says: Ruled out because "A connector cannot give anyone more access than they already have".

questions.stem: A team lead finds a handy link on a forum that would add a custom connector in seconds. What is the best step?

options.text: Install it, then watch the first few replies for anything odd
options.says: Ruled out because "Remote tools can change after you approve them", so a good first reply proves nothing about later behaviour.

options.text: Install it on the free plan first, since that permits one trial server
options.says: Ruled out because "a custom connector has not been verified by Anthropic", whatever the plan allows.

options.text: Check who operates it, and which scopes it requests, before approving
options.says: The checklist says to connect only to servers from trusted organisations and to read the scopes before approving them.

options.text: Install it in On demand mode, which restricts what the server can do
options.says: Ruled out because "the page suggests On demand when you have ten or more connectors", which is about tool loading and not about what a server may do.
